Upside down

Calving assistance
When will you intervene?
1. If the cow is restless for more than 4-6 hours but does not go into labor.
2. If a cow is straining but no part of the calf is showing after two hours.
3. If feet or nose is not showing but the calf is no delivered after 2 hours.
4. Abnormal presentation.

facts: Under normal delivery positions, presentations include 'Normal presentation' (anterior) and 'Posterior presentation'.

Abnormal delivery positions include: Transverse presentation (legs first), Transverse presentation (back first), Head back, Head to the side, Head down, Shoulder flexion, Carpal flexion, Upside down, Hock flexion, and Hip flexion.
Intervention during calving is required if the cow is restless for more than 4-6 hours but does not go into labor.
Intervention is required if a cow is straining but no part of the calf is showing after two hours.
Intervention is required if feet or nose is not showing but the calf is not delivered after 2 hours.
Intervention is required if there is an abnormal presentation.

questions.question: According to the guide, when should you intervene if a cow is restless but does not progress into active labor?

options.A: If the cow is restless for more than 1 to 2 hours
options.B: If the cow is restless for more than 4-6 hours
options.C: If the cow is restless for more than 8-10 hours
options.D: If the cow is restless for more than 12-24 hours

True or False: An abnormal presentation during calving requires human assistance or intervention.

options.A: True, abnormal presentation is an explicit condition requiring intervention.
options.B: False, all abnormal presentations correct themselves spontaneously within 6 hours.
options.C: False, intervention is only warranted after 24 hours of labor.
options.D: True, but only if the cow is a first-calf heifer.
